summary: Voyage Trend Detective is a free web tool that helps students become data detectives. The user picks a NASA variable (air temperature, wind speed, rainfall, humidity, sunlight or surface pressure) and a sea region, such as the Strait of Malacca or the English Channel. The tool downloads 31 years (1995-2025) of NASA POWER data, plots yearly averages, measures the rate of change per decade, and tests whether the trend is statistically significant using the Mann-Kendall test. It then explains the result in plain language, including when there is no significant trend.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Voyage Trend Detective is a free web tool for the challenge "Be an Earth System Trend Detective". The user picks a NASA variable (air temperature, wind speed, rainfall, relative humidity, sunlight at the surface, or surface pressure) and a sea region (nine shipping regions, or any latitude and longitude). The tool downloads monthly NASA POWER data for 1995-2025, averages it by year so the seasonal cycle does not distort the result, and draws the time series with a trend line. It reports the rate of change per decade (Sen slope) and tests whether the trend is significant using the Mann-Kendall test (significant when p < 0.05). It then explains the result in plain language and says clearly when there is no significant trend.

EXAMPLE RESULTS

Strait of Malacca, air temperature: +0.281 degrees C per decade, p < 0.001, a significant increase. English Channel, wind speed: -0.040 m/s per decade, p = 0.395, no significant trend. Showing both helps users see the difference between a real trend and normal year-to-year variation.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

The tool helps students and members of the public with some science background learn how to investigate Earth data: choose a variable, choose a place, and check whether a change is real or could be chance. Plain definitions of each variable and three example questions make it beginner friendly. It works in any web browser with nothing to install.

TOOLS USED

HTML, CSS and JavaScript for the web tool; the NASA POWER web service for data; GitHub for the code and GitHub Pages for hosting. Python (requests, pandas, numpy, matplotlib) scripts in the repository download and analyze wind data along three shipping routes. No special hardware was used.

CREATIVITY

Sea regions and shipping routes give the trend analysis a clear story: wind, temperature and rain affect ships, ports and coastal communities. Each result comes with a plain-language verdict instead of only numbers.

FACTORS CONSIDERED

We chose yearly averages and a non-parametric test so the method is simple and does not assume a normal distribution. Limitations: the tool only tests steady one-direction trends, it uses the NASA grid cell nearest the chosen point, and about 31 yearly values mean noisy records may show no significant trend.

FUTURE WORK

Add more NASA datasets (for example ocean variables), daily data, and map views.

CODE AND LIVE TOOL

https://github.com/jawaharkmea-ops/voyage-trend-detective

https://jawaharkmea-ops.github.io/voyage-trend-detective/dashboard/
